text:
nina: new hire hit a weird combo: quickstart shows an async snippet but the sample app in repo is sync and also reads credentials from ~/.config/redwood/creds.json. on Windows their CI kept failing with JSONDecodeError.

 tom: hmm. can you paste the doc snippet and the sample app lines?

 nina: docs page has:```python
async def main():
    client = Client.from_env()
    resp = client.chat.generate(... )
    print(resp)
```

 nina: sample app does:```python
from redwood import Client
client = Client.open_credentials('~/.config/redwood/creds.json')
resp = client.chat.generate(...)
print(resp)
```

 anya: two issues: 1) docs uses async but doesn't await generate (missing await) and 2) sample expects a file with LF-only JSON; on Windows we had CRLF header bytes causing our file reader to choke in older stdlib utils.

 support-bot: User report: 401 then JSONDecodeError in sample. Provided repo commit id and OS info.

 tom: also Client.from_env isn't implemented to read our creds file path; it's env-only. docs claim parity that doesn't exist. that's the SDK parity bug we wanted to avoid.

 docs-bot: scanned repo: found mismatch across 3 files: docs/quickstart/python/async.md (async snippet), examples/python/sample_app.py (sync with file read), and examples/python/.env.example (mentions REDWOOD_API_KEY). Recommend: standardize on env var use for quickstart, show both sync and async examples with correct await, and add Windows note about CRLF in creds.json.

 nina: I'll open a docs PR to: - change async snippet to `await client.chat.generate(...)` and include sync alternative - update quickstart text to say "either set REDWOOD_API_KEY or place creds.json in ~/.config/redwood/creds.json" and show how Client.from_env prefers env var - add a tiny troubleshooting blurb about Windows CRLF and a one-liner to normalize: `dos2unix ~/.config/redwood/creds.json`.

 tom: SDK follow-up: add Client.from_env to try both env var and default creds file, and make file loader tolerant of CRLF BOMs. Filed SDK issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-python/issues/321

 anya: also flag a broken link the reporter hit: docs page link to examples/python/sample_app.py 404s (renamed last week). I'll add a redirect ticket and update the link in the quickstart.

 nina: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/784 includes fixes and a small CI smoke test that runs both async and sync snippets against a dummy key.

 tom: nice. can we add a lint rule to catch doc snippets that show `async def` without `await` inside? would have prevented this.

 anya: noted for DX roadmap. adding to backlog. :spiral_notepad:
